title: Segmental ROM (peak-to-peak) of intact L1-S1 spines at ±7.5 Nm, all specimens (FE, LB)

quantity.name: ROM
quantity.definition: segmental range of motion, peak-to-peak (flexion+extension, left+right lateral bending) over the 3rd cycle at ±7.5 Nm; mean ± SD of all FSUs (female and male pooled by the authors); axial rotation NOT reported pooled

source.authors: Cook DJ, Yeager MS, Cheng BC
source.sample: 42 cadaveric L1-S1 spines; 204 FSUs (91 female, 113 male); L5-S1 tracked in 36 spines; human cadaveric lumbar spines L1-S1 (T12 and sacrum potted), intact condition pooled from 6 studies of one lab
source.sex: both sexes pooled (91 F / 113 M FSUs overall)

protocol.summary: Pure moments ±7.5 Nm, sinusoidal, 0.005 Hz, 3 cycles per mode; 3rd cycle analysed; no preload reported; 6-DOF spine tester (Bose) with FE and LB gimbals; Optotrak LEDs on each vertebral body.
how_to_simulate: Model L1-S1 (T12 and sacrum potted); fix the sacrum, apply pure moment to the cranial end, no preload
Apply ±7.5 Nm in flexion-extension, lateral bending and axial rotation (3 cycles; use the 3rd)
Per level, report the full range (peak-to-peak) of the Euler angle of the upper vertebra relative to the lower one (sequence X y' z'): FE = alpha, LB = beta, AT = gamma
Compare with the pooled mean ± SD (FE and LB only; for axial rotation use the sex-specific tests, Fig 5)
protocol.notes: ROM = range (peak-to-peak) over the 3rd cycle, i.e. flexion+extension, left+right LB, left+right AT. NZ not reported. Height/weight in source: mean 66.75 in (=169.5 cm) and 215.32 lb (=97.7 kg), converted here. Per-level, per-sex n not reported (all levels: 42 spines, L5-S1 36). Per-level n = number of spines (42 for L1-L2..L4-L5, 36 for L5-S1; 4 x 42 + 36 = 204 FSUs as stated). Axial rotation: the paper gives AT ROM only by sex (Fig 5, in tests cook2015.L1S1_intact_female/male); no pooled AT value is reported. Derived for information only (NOT data, not from the paper): pooling the Fig 5 sex bars with weights 91/113 gives AT 2.62±1.38, 3.84±2.45, 4.91±2.59, 4.59±2.63, 3.88±2.33 deg (L1-L2..L5-S1); equal weights give 2.66±1.39, 3.90±2.47, 4.98±2.64, 4.72±2.69, 3.92±2.30 - the owner's AR targets (2.6±1.4, 3.9±2.4, 5.0±2.7, 4.7±2.7, 3.9±2.3) were obtained this way (FE_VALIDATION.md: "pools the female/male bars assuming equal group sizes").

extraction.from: Fig 6 (FE) and Fig 7 (LB): "Current Study" bars, mean with +1 SD error bar (captions: "Error bars represent standard deviation")
extraction.uncertainty: ±0.1 deg mean and SD (embedded 301-ppi bitmaps; Fig 6 19.16 px/deg, Fig 7 33.1 px/deg; 1-px whisker caps)
extraction.check_notes: Digitised 2026-11-13 by pixel scan of the embedded images: y axis calibrated on gridlines (Fig 6 rows 24..503 = 25..0 deg; Fig 7 rows 24..554 = 16..0 deg); mean = top of the hatched "Current Study" bar (= lower end of the black error-bar line, checked against the hatch top in 20 neighbouring columns, +/-1 px); SD = 1-px cap row minus bar top. Cross-check with the owner's targets (fe.json lumbar.*.{FE,LB}.7p5.cook2015, "Cook 2015 Figs 5-7"): FE 7.0±2.6, 7.9±2.3, 8.8±2.6, 10.7±3.5, 12.0±4.3; LB 6.8±2.1, 9.0±2.3, 9.5±2.6, 8.5±3.0, 7.2±2.5 - all within 0.1 deg except L1-L2 FE SD (2.48 here vs 2.6) - same source. Note: n-weighted pooling of the sex-specific Fig 3/4 bars (tests cook2015.L1S1_intact_female/male) gives values ~0.1-0.5 deg higher than these bars (e.g. LB L1-L2 7.24 vs 6.81), so per-level female/male counts differ from the overall 91/113 FSU ratio or the figures use different subsets; the plotted pooled values are kept as published.
